evals.name: express-api
evals.prompt: My Express API is getting hammered by bots and scrapers. Can you help protect it?
evals.expected_output: Retrieves a site key via the Arcjet CLI and writes it to .env, installs @arcjet/node, creates a shared Arcjet client with shield() in a separate file, adds detectBot() and a rate limiting rule via withRule(), calls protect() inside each route handler (not middleware), handles denied decisions with appropriate status codes (429, 403).
assertions: Retrieves an Arcjet site key via the CLI (e.g. arcjet sites get-key)
Writes ARCJET_KEY to an env file (.env or similar) — not hardcoded
Installs @arcjet/node (not @arcjet/next or @arcjet/guard)
Creates a shared Arcjet client in its own file (e.g. src/lib/arcjet.ts), not inline in the route file
Configures shield() as a base rule on the shared client
Configures detectBot() rule
Configures a rate limiting rule (slidingWindow, fixedWindow, or tokenBucket)
Calls protect() inside route handlers (not in app.use middleware)
Checks decision.isDenied() and maps reasons to appropriate status codes (429 for rate limit, 403 for bot/shield)
Does not call protect() in Express middleware

evals.name: nextjs-signup

evals.expected_output: Retrieves a site key via the Arcjet CLI and writes it to .env.local, installs @arcjet/next, creates a shared Arcjet client (lib/arcjet.ts) with shield(), uses protectSignup() (or validateEmail()+detectBot()+slidingWindow()) to combine bot detection, email validation, and rate limiting, calls protect() with email parameter inside the POST handler.
assertions: Retrieves an Arcjet site key via the CLI (e.g. arcjet sites get-key)
Writes ARCJET_KEY to .env.local (not hardcoded)
Installs @arcjet/next (not @arcjet/node or @arcjet/guard)
Creates a shared Arcjet client file (e.g. lib/arcjet.ts), not inline in the route
Configures shield() as a base rule
Uses protectSignup() or validateEmail() to block disposable / invalid emails
Configures bot detection (via protectSignup or detectBot)
Configures a rate limiting rule
Calls protect() inside the route handler — not in middleware.ts
Passes the email value to protect() (e.g. { email })
Maps denial reasons to appropriate HTTP responses

evals.name: node-agent-tools
evals.prompt: My AI agent makes tool calls and I need to rate limit per user and block prompt injection before each tool runs.
evals.expected_output: Retrieves a site key via the Arcjet CLI and writes it to .env, installs @arcjet/guard (not the request-based SDK), creates guard client at module scope with launchArcjet(), configures tokenBucket and detectPromptInjection rules, calls guard() inline in each tool function with a per-tool label (e.g. 'tools.get-weather'), uses the user id as the rate limit key, handles DENY decisions.
assertions: Retrieves an Arcjet site key via the CLI
Writes ARCJET_KEY to .env (not hardcoded)
Uses @arcjet/guard package (not @arcjet/node or @arcjet/next)
Creates the guard client with launchArcjet() at module scope (not inside a function)
Configures a rate limiting rule (tokenBucket, fixedWindow, or slidingWindow)
Configures detectPromptInjection() rule
Calls guard() inline at each tool call site with a descriptive label (e.g. 'tools.<name>')
Passes the user identifier as the rate limit key (not a hardcoded value)
Checks decision.conclusion === 'DENY' before proceeding
Does not use the HTTP SDK (@arcjet/node or @arcjet/next)

evals.expected_output: Retrieves a site key via the Arcjet CLI and writes it to an env file, adds arcjet to requirements.txt, creates a guard client at module scope using launch_arcjet (async, since this code uses AsyncOpenAI), configures a token bucket / sliding window rate limit and detect_prompt_injection rule, calls arcjet.guard() inline in handle_tool_call with a per-tool label and the user_id as the rate limit key, checks decision.conclusion for DENY.

Uses launch_arcjet (async) — not launch_arcjet_sync — since the agent uses AsyncOpenAI
Creates the guard client at module scope (not inside handle_tool_call)
Configures a rate limiting rule

Calls await arcjet.guard(...) inside handle_tool_call with a per-tool label
Uses user_id as the rate limit key (not a hardcoded value)

evals.name: python-queue-worker
evals.prompt: This worker pulls AI tasks off a queue and runs them through OpenAI. We've had cost spikes from abusive users. Add some protection.
evals.expected_output: Retrieves a site key via the Arcjet CLI and writes it to an env file, adds arcjet to requirements.txt, creates a guard client at module scope using launch_arcjet_sync (since process_task is a regular sync function), configures a token bucket rate limit keyed by user_id (and ideally detect_prompt_injection on the prompt), calls arcjet.guard() inline in process_task with a label like 'queue.process-task', uses task['user_id'] as the rate limit key, checks decision.conclusion for DENY before calling the model.
assertions: Retrieves an Arcjet site key via the CLI
Writes ARCJET_KEY to an env file (not hardcoded)
Adds arcjet to requirements.txt
Imports from arcjet.guard
Uses launch_arcjet_sync (sync) — not launch_arcjet — since process_task is a sync function
Creates the guard client at module scope
Configures a rate limiting rule
Calls arcjet.guard() inside process_task with a descriptive label (e.g. 'queue.process-task')
Uses task['user_id'] as the rate limit key
Checks decision.conclusion for DENY before calling the OpenAI client
